analysis.title: The AI boom is starting to crack in unexpected places
key_insights: KOSPI fell 3-4% and Samsung and SK Hynix fell around 4%, while Taiwan was broadly flat. Memory is the epicenter of the weakness.
CXMT unveiled a new 4F² DRAM architecture over the weekend. China already accounts for roughly 10% of global DRAM revenues and is expanding capacity.
Near-term memory fundamentals remain very strong, but investors are questioning whether peak memory profitability is approaching and are trading expected revisions rather than past earnings.
Samsung's results did not deliver the large upside surprise investors had positioned for, which added to the unwind.

KOSPI broke below the bigger trend line late last week and the overnight drop took it to its 200-day moving average, a level tested only once since the rally began. A decisive close below it risks further losses.

KOSPI VIX had been in a vol-reset mode since the market topped, but spiked overnight. Volatility barely reacted for much of the correction, which suggests the market is now pricing genuine downside risk.
Buybacks in KOSPI are going into hibernation. They were an important source of support through the rally, and the bid is fading as technical damage accelerates.
SK Hynix broke below a triangle-like formation and trades below its 100-day moving average but above its 200-day. With buyback support fading, the author sees it as dead money at best.
Samsung shows a similar pattern with less downside momentum. It reversed at the 100-day moving average and is threatening to break below the triangle, with the 200-day much lower.
The KOSPI vs SOX divergence keeps widening. Korea is pricing peak memory earnings while US semis trade the structural AI growth story. The author doubts the divergence can persist indefinitely.

Korea is essentially a leveraged bet on the memory cycle, while Taiwan is dominated by TSMC and advanced semiconductor manufacturing. The market questions memory profit sustainability while still rewarding AI infrastructure.
